messages:
incidents-bot: :pager: PAGER: Alert alert-ml-782 — model-load failures on prod-us-east-1 (inference-serving). Multiple warmup errors reported: OOM at load, CUDA OOM, deserialization errors, and compile timeouts. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/model-load-failures. Paging oncall.

Maya: ack, I'm on it. I see a cluster-wide spike in model warmup failures for `llama-13b-v2` on nodes in us-east-1.

Maya: quick tail of loader logs from pod inference-llama13b-0:
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] ERROR runtime: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.2 GiB (GPU 0; 15.90 GiB total; 14.50 GiB already allocated)
[2026-03-15T09:12:05Z] WARN model: failed to deserialize object at offset 0x1f2b3
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"/app/loader.py\", line 234, in load_weights
    state_dict = torch.load(f, map_location='cuda')
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory\n```

Sriram: I'm seeing repeated `Graph compile timed out after 30s` from the XLA backend on several containers right before the OOM. Looks like compile + deserialization > warmup timeout. Also noticed `async-weights-load=true` in env for that model.

Josh: oncall here — paging infra. @Anita @Sriram can you confirm node flapping? I'm setting an immediate mitigation: divert traffic to fallback models and start draining problematic node(s).

Anita: Confirmed. Node i-0abcd1234 in us-east-1 is restarting kubelet and containers repeatedly. Container logs show OOM at model load, then kube restarts container. Suspect memory spike on warmup triggers OOM, container restarts create thrash.

Anita: Mitigations I'm running now:
- cordon & drain node:
`kubectl cordon i-0abcd1234`
`kubectl drain i-0abcd1234 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
- increase model warmup timeout for `llama-13b-v2` to 90s in serving config (to allow compile to finish)
- temporarily reduce `batch_size` for that model from 8 -> 4 to lower peak memory
- kick off rollout of quantized variant (4-bit) to absorb some traffic:
`redwoodctl models rollout --model llama-13b-v2-quant --traffic 50% --region us-east-1`

Maya: pushed a change to disable `continuous_prefetch` for that model to reduce prefetch memory pressure. Also uploaded debug dump: s3://redwood-debug/prod-us-east-1/llama13b/warmup-dumps/1772504321.tar.gz

Devin (Support): We're seeing customer errors — about 12 tenants in us-east-1 reporting 502/timeout on generation endpoints between 09:10–09:20 UTC. Any ETA for mitigation? Need a short customer-facing update.

Josh: Short update for customers: "We're investigating elevated errors for some models in us-east-1 due to model warmup failures; routing and mitigations in progress. We'll follow up in 30m with status and mitigation summary." Use that as a template, add affected tenants list from the support dashboard.

Sriram: Root causes observed so far:
- async weights load + aggressive prefetching -> simultaneous allocations at load time
- compile phase (kernel selection/graph compile) taking >30s on some instances -> exceeds warmup timeout and leaves partial allocations
- quantized variant not yet primarily used so memory footprint higher than expected

Action items I'm doing now:
- Disable `async-weights-load` for the model (hotfix env var)
- Increase `MODEL_SERIALIZE_TIMEOUT` to 120s to prevent premature kill during compile
- Add a short-term auto-fallback rule: when model-load failures > 5% in 1m, route new requests to `llama-7b`

Maya: After the rollouts and env toggles, I'm seeing decreased OOMs on nodes we've drained. Traffic is successfully routed to quant variant and to `llama-7b` fallback for canary tenants. Latency is slightly higher on fallback but success rate increased.

Anita: Continuing monitoring. I'll keep the node drained until we can repro reliably on a dev cluster and patch the loader. Also creating a ticket to increase instance GPU memory for that flavor in the long term or change the warmup strategy.

Josh: I'm going to start a formal handoff in 30m to @Anita — summarizing: initial pager for model-load OOMs -> found async loads + compile timeouts -> drained node, rolled quantized model, reduced batch size, increased warmup timeout, disabled prefetch, set fallback routing. Current state: mitigations in effect, error rate down from ~18% -> ~1.2%.

Anita: Taking over. Will update the incident bridge and start postmortem draft. Please add any logs/links to the postmortem doc: https://redwood/incidents/1772504321-postmortem.

incidents-bot: Incident status: mitigation_in_progress. Metric: model_warmup_fail_rate_us_east_1 decreased to 1.2% (was 18%). Next check-in scheduled +30m.

Maya: quick note — hypothesis for postmortem: weight serialization/deserialization code path doesn't gracefully free partial allocations on failure. We'll add guards and ensure loader pre-checks free memory before retry.

Devin (Support): Copy — I'll push a customer update now referencing the short update and will follow up with impacted tenant list.

Anita: will continue monitoring, update when we mark resolved. Leaving a checklist for postmortem: reproduce in staging, fix loader alloc cleanup, add model warmup SLOs, evaluate instance type / quant adoption.

Josh: thanks all. handing off to Anita (oncall). :thumbsup:
